Per-crate landed; workspace decision deferred. Commit: 7697b7c.
description:
## Hypothesis

`ContactCard`, `AddressBook`, and the 30+ re-exported RFC 9553 JSContact sub-types (`Name`, `EmailAddress`, `Phone`, `Address`, `OnlineService`, `Note`, `Anniversary`, `PersonalInfo`, `CryptoKey` (which holds a URI, not raw key bytes), etc.) all `#[derive(Debug)]`. None of them have a redacting `Debug` impl.

A downstream consumer writing:

```rust
tracing::debug!(card = ?contact_card, "fetched contact");
```

emits every phone number, email address, postal address, given/surname, note text, and CryptoKey URI to whatever logging sink `tracing` is wired to (stderr, journald, a SIEM, S3, CloudWatch...). This is **PII leakage** by default. The data here is not credential-grade in the strict sense (Section A scope) but is regulated under GDPR Article 5, CCPA §1798.100, and most privacy frameworks as personally-identifying.

## Workspace precedent

The workspace **does** have a Debug-redaction pattern documented in `AGENTS.md` 'Security testing':

> Per-type Debug redaction canary — a unit test that constructs the type with a canary literal under the test's control and asserts the canary does not appear in `format!("{value:?}")` output.

And the pattern is **applied** in `jmap-base-client` to credential and account types: `BearerAuth`, `BasicAuth`, `Session` (request.rs:244), `AccountInfo` (request.rs:340). The redaction comment in request.rs:335 explicitly mentions 'this redaction closes the transitive leak through Session.accounts'.

But the workspace pattern has **not** propagated to any sibling type crate: `jmap-mail-types` (Email, EmailAddress, EmailHeader) derives plain Debug; `jmap-jscontact-types` derives plain Debug; `jmap-calendars-types` derives plain Debug; `jmap-chat-types` derives plain Debug. This is a **workspace-wide gap**, surfaced concretely by the contacts review because contacts data is the cleanest example of programmatic PII.

## What goes wrong

A downstream consumer using `tracing` to instrument their JMAP server logs PII at debug level by default. The leak is:

- Silent: no compile-time signal, no test failure.
- Wide: `Debug` is the default formatter for `?` in macros across the Rust ecosystem.
- Privacy-impacting: GDPR/CCPA reporting obligations if the log sink is breached.

The defense `jmap-base-client` ships for credential types — a manual `impl Debug` that prints the type name and field count without contents — should propagate to PII-bearing types. The decision is policy-level: should the workspace redact PII by default in Debug, or document the leak and require consumers to wrap?

## Three options

**(a) Workspace-wide policy decision, deferred**: File a workspace bead to decide whether type crates should redact PII in `Debug` by default, and propagate to all sibling type crates if yes. Per-crate work waits on the workspace decision.

**(b) Crate-scoped redaction**: Add manual `Debug` impls to `ContactCard`, `AddressBook`, and the 22 sloppy-field re-exports that redact value content. Add the `Debug` canary test pattern. Single crate, paves the way for the workspace sweep.

**(c) Docs-only contract**: Add a top-level crate doc-comment titled `# Logging safety` warning consumers that all types derive plain `Debug` and `tracing::debug!(?card)` leaks PII. Document the recommended consumer-side wrapper pattern.

## Acceptance criteria

The bead is sized for **(c) docs-only** unless the workspace policy bead (a sub-task of this) decides otherwise. Concrete acceptance:

1. Add `# Logging safety` section to `src/lib.rs` top-level crate docs.
2. Section wording (template):

   > This crate derives plain `Debug` on all PII-bearing types (`ContactCard`, `AddressBook`, `Name`, `EmailAddress`, `Phone`, `Address`, `Note`, ...). Consumers using `tracing` or `log` macros that interpolate values via `?` (debug) or `%` (display) emit the full record contents to the configured sink. This includes phone numbers, email addresses, postal addresses, names, notes, and CryptoKey URIs — all of which are typically regulated as personally-identifying information.
   > 
   > Consumers SHOULD wrap PII-bearing types in a redacting newtype before logging, or use a structured-logging field-allowlist (e.g. `tracing::debug!(card_id = %card.id.as_ref().unwrap_or(&Id::from("<absent>")), "fetched")`) that emits only the `id` and never the body.

3. Cross-reference workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' and `jmap-base-client`'s redacting-Debug precedent.

## Probe / downstream session

A downstream `/do-beads JMAP-glx8` session under appropriate permissions:

1. Add the `# Logging safety` section to lib.rs:1-63 (the existing crate-level doc).
2. Verify `cargo doc --no-deps -p jmap-contacts-types` renders cleanly.
3. File a workspace bead `Type-crate Debug redaction policy decision` that asks whether sibling type crates should propagate `jmap-base-client`'s redacting-Debug pattern to all PII-bearing types workspace-wide. The decision blocks any (b)-grade per-crate work.

## Cross-reference

- Workspace AGENTS.md 'Security testing' — Debug redaction canary pattern + log-capture canary pattern.
- crate-jmap-base-client/src/request.rs:244, :340 — the manual-Debug redaction precedent (Session, AccountInfo).
- crate-jmap-base-client/tests/log_redaction.rs — the log-capture canary test.

This is filed P3 (hygiene) rather than P2 because (i) the leak requires a downstream consumer to actually wire a debug-level logger that interpolates the type, (ii) the workspace has the precedent but explicitly only applied it to credential types so the current scope is consistent with workspace policy, (iii) PII vs credential-secret is a meaningful distinction. P2 would be appropriate if the workspace decides yes on (a).
title: PII-bearing types derive plain Debug; downstream tracing::debug!(?card) leaks contact data
